writeup.headline: Akamai rates Hold: steady cash generation and AI-cloud deals offset by slow growth, debt and weak price trend.
writeup.thesis: Akamai scores 48, a Hold, only 4 points above the Sell line. Growth is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 5.9% and growth slowed by 0.4 pp from the previous quarter, and the balance sheet scores weakly with net debt at 4.4x FCF and cash covering 0.44 of debt. Quality is middling: a 22.1% FCF margin is solid, but stock-based compensation is 11.8% of revenue and the diluted share count is up 5.8% year on year. On absolute levels, P/S of 3.3x and P/FCF of 14.7x look moderate while EV/EBIT of 40.2x is high, and the FCF yield is 1.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history, valuation sits near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S cheap, P/FCF middle, EV/EBIT expensive). The price trend is weak, with the price 12.8% below its 200-day average and 39.1% below its 52-week high.
key_risks: Heavy reliance on one large customer through the Anthropic cloud deal, which makes up much of the more than $14B of multiyear contracts
Leverage, with net debt at 4.4x FCF and cash covering only 0.44 of debt
Ongoing dilution, with the diluted share count up 5.8% year on year and SBC at 11.8% of revenue
Analysts cutting price targets, and shares 10.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days
Q3 results on November 5 could disappoint against the narrowed FY26 guidance
what_would_change: A drop of more than 4 points in the score, from weaker growth, further price declines or more negative analyst news, would move the rating to Sell
Reaching Buy needs 17 more points, likely requiring faster revenue growth and a recovering price trend
Strong Q3 results on November 5 showing the AI cloud contracts lifting revenue would help the growth and news factors
Paying down debt or a lower net debt to FCF ratio would lift the balance sheet score
